title: AI Usage
description: Unified cross-provider AI spend/usage dashboard -- Claude Code (real $, native cost telemetry) + Codex (ESTIMATED $ at API list price -- runs on a ChatGPT Plan Pro subscription with no real cost telemetry, see provisioning/prometheus/codex-price-table.md). Real and estimated dollars are NEVER summed into one number anywhere on this dashboard -- always separate panels/series, always labeled. Built on the ai:tokens:sum / ai:tool_calls:sum / ai:cost_usd:sum canonical recording rules (provisioning/prometheus/recording-rules.yml) plus Loki panels for signals that don't exist in Prometheus yet (Codex headless tokens/cost). Designed to take a third provider (e.g. OpenRouter) by adding a recording-rule leg -- see the design note row at the bottom.

panels.title: AI Usage — Overview (reported vs calculated spend, kept separate)
Claude Spend (reported)

This is a subscription account (acct1..6 rotation), which has no per-token bill -- "reported" is a common list-price yardstick, not a charge.

panels.title: Extending to a third provider (e.g. OpenRouter)

options.content:
### Adding `provider="openrouter"` (or any new provider) to this schema

The `ai:tokens:sum` / `ai:tool_calls:sum` / `ai:cost_usd:sum` recording rules
(`provisioning/prometheus/recording-rules.yml`) are additive per provider --
a new provider needs **its own rule block per metric**, following the
existing `anthropic`/`openai` pattern:

```yaml
- record: ai:tokens:sum
  labels:
    provider: openrouter
  expr: |
    sum by (model, token_type, project, branch, linear_key, task_type, account, phase) (
      <openrouter's native token-usage metric>
    )
```

**For a new provider to show up correctly across this whole dashboard**, its
OTLP exporter needs to emit, on whichever metric(s) carry token/cost data:

| canonical label | what to stamp | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `model` | the model id string | e.g. `glm-4.6`, `kimi-k2` |
| `token_type` (or a label `label_replace`-able to it) | `input` / `output` / `cached` / ... | match the OpenAI/Anthropic token_type vocabulary where possible |
| `project` / `branch` / `linear_key` / `task_type` | same `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` the relay dispatcher already sets for Claude/Codex | `~/catalyst/comms/coord/relay-dispatch.sh` is the one place that needs a new `--settings`/env block per provider |
| `account` / `phase` | same dispatcher-stamped attrs | only useful once the recording rule groups by them (already done here) |
| a REAL cost metric, if the provider bills per-token (OpenRouter does) | `<provider>_cost_usd_total` or equivalent | if real $ exist, wire a real `ai:cost_usd:sum` leg -- do NOT fall back to an estimated/list-price leg when a real number is available |

Once the metric exists with those labels, this dashboard's panels need **one
line each**: add an `{"expr": ..., "legendFormat": "openrouter"}` target
to the "by Provider" panels above (`Tool Calls by Provider`, `Tokens by
Provider`, `Spend Trend by Provider`) -- the per-dimension panels
(`Spend by Model`/`by Ticket`/`by Project`/...) don't need changes if they
already query the unified `ai:*` recording rule name (the `provider` label
just gets a new value automatically).

panels.title: Subscription Efficiency — retail-$ per subscription-window (Ryan's Task C)

options.content:
### Read this before trusting these numbers

**Directional, not billing truth.** Neither number is a real marginal dollar -- both are list-price valuations of usage that differ only in who computed them (Claude Code reports its own; we calculate Codex's from tokens). They exist as a common yardstick for the efficiency quotient below, not as bills. Both providers are flat-rate subscriptions
($200/mo-class) -- there is no per-token bill to reconcile against. This row
answers "how many retail-priced dollars of work does each subscription
window deliver" as a **relative efficiency signal**, not a real cost.

- **Numerator** (retail-$): `claude_code_cost_usage_USD_total` is Claude
  Code's own list-price approximation -- verified 2026-08-24 by cross-checking
  a real session's token counts against Anthropic's published API pricing
  (computed $216.12 vs Claude Code's reported $229.56, within ~6%, consistent
  with the SAME pricing basis -- see recording-rules.yml for the worked
  example). Codex's numerator is the Task A ESTIMATED-cost series (same
  list-price logic, Loki-only -- see the two panels below).
- **Denominator** (limit consumed): neither provider exports this as OTLP.
  `ai_subscription_limit_used_percent` is a NEW gauge fed by
  `scripts/ai-subscription-limit-scraper.sh` (proven live end-to-end
  2026-08-24) -- not yet reflected in Prometheus until the collector config
  is deployed (restart required).
- **Limit-charging weights are opaque.** A model that looks "cheap per
  limit-%" here might be internally weighted differently against the actual
  subscription quota than its published token price implies -- Anthropic/
  OpenAI do not publish that mapping.
- **Reset-boundary handling**: the ratio uses a rolling `[5h]`/`[7d]` lookback,
  not a window strictly aligned to `resets_at`. Right after a reset,
  `used_percent` drops to ~0 while the rolling $ window still includes
  pre-reset spend -- the ratio will read artificially high in that gap.
  Cross-check `resets_at` (carried on every subscription-limit sample) before
  trusting a ratio near a reset boundary.

- **Claude has NO historical subscription-limit data, anywhere, ever.** The
  5h/7d `used_percent` this dashboard reads (`catalyst-stack claude-account
  status` / `claude-accounts-usage.mjs --json`) is a LIVE snapshot of
  CURRENT usage from Anthropic's OAuth usage endpoint -- it has no history
  API and this fleet has never logged past readings anywhere. The
  Subscription Efficiency panels above only have Claude data from whenever
  `scripts/ai-subscription-limit-scraper.sh`'s cron started sampling it
  (2026-08-24) forward. If you're looking for what Claude's limit usage
  looked like last week, it does not exist -- don't go hunting for it.
- **Codex DOES have bounded history** (`scripts/codex-limit-history-replay.sh`,
  one-shot, already run 2026-08-24): its rollout JSONLs carry a
  `rate_limits` snapshot on every turn, going back to 2025-09-16 on this
  laptop -- but Loki's out-of-order ingestion window caps what's actually
  queryable at ~7 days back from whenever the replay runs (168h, Loki's
  default `reject_old_samples_max_age`, measured empirically -- not
  overridable after the fact). The 2026-08-24 replay landed 60 of 82
  candidate samples spanning 2026-08-19 through 2026-08-24 (some data loss
  from Loki's per-stream ingestion ordering, not from the 168h cutoff
  itself -- see the script's comments).

panels.description: (retail-$ spent in the trailing 5h) / (used_percent of the 5h window) * 100 -- 'if this account fully consumed its 5h window at the observed rate, this is roughly what it would be worth at API list price.' NOT YET LIVE -- needs ai_subscription_limit_used_percent deployed (see collector-config.yaml). Query-equivalent verified 2026-08-24: acct6 spent $23.38 retail in 5h at 62% used -> $37.71/full-window.

panels.description: Same formula as the 5h panel, 7-day window. NOT YET LIVE -- needs ai_subscription_limit_used_percent deployed.

A LOW value means that model's retail-priced work consumes subscription limit fast relative to its list price -- i.e. it 'burns limit fastest per dollar of output.' Directional only -- see the caveat panel above. NOT YET LIVE -- needs ai_subscription_limit_used_percent deployed.

panels.title: Codex: Spend (calculated), trailing 7d (numerator)

targets.expr: (sum(sum_over_time({service_name="codex_exec"} | event_name="codex.sse_event" | model="gpt-5.6-sol" | unwrap input_token_count [7d])) - sum(sum_over_time({service_name="codex_exec"} | event_name="codex.sse_event" | model="gpt-5.6-sol" | unwrap cached_token_count [7d]))) * 0.000004 + sum(sum_over_time({service_name="codex_exec"} | event_name="codex.sse_event" | model="gpt-5.6-sol" | unwrap cached_token_count [7d])) * 0.0000004 + sum(sum_over_time({service_name="codex_exec"} | event_name="codex.sse_event" | model="gpt-5.6-sol" | unwrap output_token_count [7d])) * 0.00002

Divide by the panel to the right (used_percent/100) by hand for the Codex efficiency ratio -- Grafana can't natively divide a Loki series by a Prometheus series in one panel; see the design note.

panels.title: Codex: Subscription Limit Used, 7d window (denominator)
panels.description: NOT YET LIVE -- needs ai_subscription_limit_used_percent deployed. Query-equivalent verified 2026-08-24: this laptop's single Codex account read 27.0% used of its 7-day window.

panels.title: Codex efficiency: how to combine the two panels above

options.content:
**Codex retail-$ per full 7d window (calculated)** = (Spend/calculated panel value) / (Used-Percent panel value / 100).

Example from the 2026-08-24 verification run: $68.70 calculated spend at 27.0% of the 7-day window used -> **~$254.40 per full window** at the observed rate.

Not computed as a single Grafana panel on purpose: the numerator lives in Loki (Codex headless has no native Prometheus token-usage metric, see dashboards/codex-usage.json) and the denominator lives in Prometheus (the new subscription-limit gauge) -- combining a Loki series and a Prometheus series in one panel needs a Grafana Mixed-datasource transform that could not be visually verified in this environment (API-only access, no rendered browser). Two clearly-labeled panels side by side is honest and correct; a true combined panel is a good follow-up once someone can verify it renders.

`phase` is a resource attribute the relay dispatcher only started stamping on
sessions dispatched after ~13:00 today (2026-08-24) -- unlabeled sessions are
excluded from every panel below, not blended into an "unknown" bucket (same
rule as the account/phase panels above). Today's data will only show whatever
phases have actually run since then (e.g. implement/validate/plan/research) --
that's real sparse coverage building up over time, not a bug. "Phase RUNS"
counts every distinct session/conversation that started in that phase,
**including failed or re-dispatched ones** -- this is throughput, not
completions. A real "$ per COMPLETED phase" metric needs a completion-event
contract (see the design note panel below) that doesn't exist yet.

panels.title: Claude Phase Runs (session count, not completions)
panels.description: Distinct session_id per phase. A run that failed or was re-dispatched still counts -- this is throughput, not completions.

panels.title: Codex Phase Runs (conversation count, not completions)

targets.expr: sort_desc(count by (phase) (count by (phase, conversation_id) (count_over_time({service_name="codex_exec"} | event_name="codex.conversation_starts" | phase!="" [$__range]))))

panels.description: Distinct conversation_id per phase, counted via codex.conversation_starts (sparse, low-cardinality event -- avoids Loki's 500-series query cap that a raw stream count hits).

panels.title: Claude: $ per Phase-Run (reported)

targets.expr: sort_desc(sum by (phase) (max_over_time(claude_code_cost_usage_USD_total{phase!=""}[$__range])) / on (phase) count by (phase) (count by (phase, session_id) (max_over_time(claude_code_token_usage_tokens_total{phase!=""}[$__range]))))

panels.description: REPORTED $ (Claude Code's own API-list-price computation) divided by phase-run count. What a research/plan/implement/validate run costs on Claude, per unit of work.

panels.title: Codex: $ per Phase-Run (calculated)

targets.expr: ((sum by (phase) (sum_over_time({service_name="codex_exec"} | event_name="codex.sse_event" | model="gpt-5.6-sol" | phase!="" | unwrap input_token_count [$__range])) - sum by (phase) (sum_over_time({service_name="codex_exec"} | event_name="codex.sse_event" | model="gpt-5.6-sol" | phase!="" | unwrap cached_token_count [$__range]))) * 0.000004 + sum by (phase) (sum_over_time({service_name="codex_exec"} | event_name="codex.sse_event" | model="gpt-5.6-sol" | phase!="" | unwrap cached_token_count [$__range])) * 0.0000004 + sum by (phase) (sum_over_time({service_name="codex_exec"} | event_name="codex.sse_event" | model="gpt-5.6-sol" | phase!="" | unwrap output_token_count [$__range])) * 0.00002) / on (phase) count by (phase) (count by (phase, conversation_id) (count_over_time({service_name="codex_exec"} | event_name="codex.conversation_starts" | phase!="" [$__range])))

panels.description: CALCULATED $ (API list price) divided by phase-run count. Same list-price-per-unit-of-work idea as the Claude panel, computed the other way (Loki-native since Codex's numerator has no Prometheus series).

panels.title: Claude: Tokens per Phase-Run

targets.expr: sort_desc(sum by (phase) (max_over_time(claude_code_token_usage_tokens_total{phase!=""}[$__range])) / on (phase) count by (phase) (count by (phase, session_id) (max_over_time(claude_code_token_usage_tokens_total{phase!=""}[$__range]))))

panels.description: Provider-neutral throughput variant of the $-per-phase-run panel.

panels.title: Codex: Tokens per Phase-Run

targets.expr: (sum by (phase) (sum_over_time({service_name="codex_exec"} | event_name="codex.sse_event" | phase!="" | unwrap input_token_count [$__range])) + sum by (phase) (sum_over_time({service_name="codex_exec"} | event_name="codex.sse_event" | phase!="" | unwrap output_token_count [$__range]))) / on (phase) count by (phase) (count by (phase, conversation_id) (count_over_time({service_name="codex_exec"} | event_name="codex.conversation_starts" | phase!="" [$__range])))

panels.description: Provider-neutral throughput variant of the $-per-phase-run panel.

panels.title: Design note: completion-event contract (for the coordinator to implement)

options.content:
Sessions can't tell DONE from FAILED on their own -- the panels above
count RUNS (throughput), not completions. The coordinator verifies every
relay report already, so it's the right place to emit a terminal outcome
event once per verified report.

**Proposed contract** (OTLP log, same transport as
`scripts/ai-subscription-limit-scraper.sh` -- `http://100.65.193.30:4318/v1/logs`):

- `event_name`: `relay.phase.completed` (matches this repo's existing
  `phase.*`/`catalyst.*` event-naming convention)
- attributes (all snake_case log-record attributes, matching every other
  event in this schema):
  - `linear_key` -- the ticket (e.g. `CTC-970`)
  - `phase` -- `research`/`plan`/`implement`/`validate`/`pr`/...
  - `provider` -- `anthropic`/`openai`
  - `model`
  - `account` -- the fleet rotation slot (`acct6`) or Codex account id
  - `outcome` -- `done` | `failed` | `blocked`
  - `duration_s`
  - `project` -- **not** `repo`: this repo's existing convention (every
    `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` emitter, `use_otel_context`, the dispatcher)
    already calls this dimension `project`; introducing `repo` as a second
    spelling of the same thing would fragment queries across two label
    names for no reason. Use `project` to match everything else.

**New signal_to_metrics rule** (collector-config.yaml, once the emitter
exists): `ai_phase_completion_total`, a `count`-connector occurrence
counter keyed on `event_name=="relay.phase.completed"`, attributes
`phase`, `provider`, `model`, `outcome`, `account` -- LOW-CARD ONLY,
deliberately NOT `linear_key`/`project` (matches this repo's existing
cardinality rule for connector-derived metrics: ticket-level breakdowns
stay on Loki, aggregate counters stay low-card on Prometheus). Once live,
add `ai:phase_completions:sum` to recording-rules.yml the same way as
`ai:tool_calls:sum`, and a "$ per COMPLETED phase" panel here dividing
the phase-$ panels above by `ai:phase_completions:sum{outcome="done"}`.

**Worked emit example** (once the endpoint/format is confirmed against a
real collector run, same shape as `ai.subscription_limit.sampled` in
`scripts/ai-subscription-limit-scraper.sh`):

```json
POST http://100.65.193.30:4318/v1/logs
{
  "resourceLogs": [{
    "resource": {"attributes": [
      {"key": "service.name", "value": {"stringValue": "catalyst-coordinator"}}
    ]},
    "scopeLogs": [{
      "scope": {"name": "relay_phase_completion"},
      "logRecords": [{
        "timeUnixNano": "<epoch ns>",
        "severityNumber": 9, "severityText": "INFO",
        "body": {"stringValue": "relay.phase.completed"},
        "attributes": [
          {"key": "event_name", "value": {"stringValue": "relay.phase.completed"}},
          {"key": "linear_key", "value": {"stringValue": "CTC-970"}},
          {"key": "phase", "value": {"stringValue": "implement"}},
          {"key": "provider", "value": {"stringValue": "anthropic"}},
          {"key": "model", "value": {"stringValue": "claude-sonnet-5"}},
          {"key": "account", "value": {"stringValue": "acct6"}},
          {"key": "outcome", "value": {"stringValue": "done"}},
          {"key": "duration_s", "value": {"doubleValue": 842.0}},
          {"key": "project", "value": {"stringValue": "catalyst-cloud"}}
        ]
      }]
    }]
  }]
}
```

Once you (the coordinator) wire this in, ping back and I'll add the
recording rule + the "$ per COMPLETED phase" panel.
